scenarios.name: phishing-lateral
scenarios.title: Phishing to lateral movement
scenarios.summary: A finance user follows a credential-phishing link. Network telemetry cannot see the click; the mesh first sees ws-fin-07 pull a second stage, then sweep the file server, then a burst of logins against it from the IT jump host using harvested admin credentials.
walkthrough: Launch. Three flows arrive; triage escalates each, investigation cites the raw log lines and ATT&CK, containment proposes an action for each.
Approve isolating ws-fin-07 (10.20.4.17) — the foothold.
Decide the block of 10.20.4.17 raised by the discovery sweep; it is redundant once the host is isolated, so rejecting it is reasonable.

Approve blocking 10.20.0.5. The router refuses it: the jump host is protected infrastructure. The run completes with a FAILED action and the refusal reason — the guardrail firing where you can see it.
Open the audit timeline: every approval names you, and the chain verifies.

scenarios.name: vendor-cve
scenarios.title: Vendor-dependency CVE
scenarios.summary: Four CVEs are disclosed together in an archived package that sits four hops below several organisations, inside their vendors' dependency trees — the exposure no vendor questionnaire reaches. The same morning, the Code-Scan Agent reviews acme/billing and maps its findings to CVEs.
walkthrough: Launch. The advisory lands on the graph; the GNN re-scores it and the Supply-Chain Agent reviews everything the package reaches.
Open the supply-chain map: the fourth-order path from the package to each organisation is drawn, and every flag cites the path that drove it.
Approve the remediation: a tracking issue is opened in GitHub (the dependency change itself is not invented — the graph is synthetic).
Open the code-scan view: read the draft PR body and diff, then approve. The PR is opened as a draft and never merged.

scenarios.name: malicious-package
scenarios.title: Malicious open-source package
scenarios.summary: A widely used, long-abandoned package changes hands and ships a release that steals CI secrets. ci-runner-03 installed it: its install script posts the build environment to an external host, and the request carries a note addressed to AI security scanners asking them not to escalate.
walkthrough: Launch. The MAL advisory re-scores the graph; the exfiltration flow from ci-runner-03 enters the incident graph.
Open the incident: the payload's note to 'AI scanners' is flagged as a prompt injection and forced to escalate — it is shown as inert text.
Approve isolating ci-runner-03 (10.20.8.30).
Approve the supply-chain remediation for the package; review its reach on the map.

pending_action.rationale: Policy chose escalate (confidence 0.41) for a high alert triaged escalate and mapped to T1110. Proposed action: block_ip.

evidence.excerpt: Repeated authentication attempts to discover valid credentials, whether by guessing many passwords against one account, one common password against many accounts, or replaying credential pairs leaked elsewhere.

Count failures per source and per account over a sliding window, and count distinct accounts attempted per source. The spraying variant is invisible to per-account lockout thresholds, so distinct-account fan-out is the signal that catches it.
Trying a small number of likely passwords across a large number of accounts, staying below per-account lockout thresholds while still succeeding somewhere in a large directory.
Replay of username and password pairs harvested from unrelated breaches against the victim's services, exploiting password reuse rather than any weakness in the target.

queue0.caption: Internal discovery sweep from ws-fin-07 against fs-01

pending_action.rationale: Policy chose escalate (confidence 0.38) for a medium alert triaged escalate and mapped to T1046. Proposed action: block_ip.

evidence.excerpt: Scanning inside the network to find reachable services and versions, which is how an adversary converts a single foothold into a map of exploitable targets.

Internal source addresses contacting many destination ports or many destination hosts with a high proportion of failed handshakes. East-west flow records are the right telemetry; perimeter logs never see this.

Discovery activity is individually benign and collectively decisive. A workstation enumerating hosts, shares, accounts and privileged groups within a few minutes is either a security tool, an administrator with a script, or an intruder orienting after initial access, and the three are easy to separate by asking who owns the source.

pending_action.rationale: Policy chose escalate (confidence 0.31) for a critical alert triaged escalate and mapped to T1105. Proposed action: isolate_host.

evidence.excerpt: Transfer of tooling into the environment from outside after initial access, commonly using built-in download utilities so nothing unusual needs to be present first.
Built-in transfer utilities invoked with external URLs by non-administrative parents, and executable content written immediately after an outbound connection to a low-reputation host.

Command and control hides in permitted protocols, so the discriminator is the pattern rather than the destination. Interval regularity, small and uniform request sizes and a single internal client per destination are the durable signals; domain reputation is a weak one because adversaries increasingly use well-reputed hosting and legitimate services.

The same morning, the Code-Scan Agent reviews acme/billing and maps its findings to CVEs.
walkthrough: Launch. The advisory lands on the graph; the GNN re-scores it and the Supply-Chain Agent reviews everything the package reaches.
Open the supply-chain map: the fourth-order path from the package to each organisation is drawn, and every flag cites the path that drove it.
Approve the remediation: a tracking issue is opened in GitHub (the dependency change itself is not invented — the graph is synthetic).
Open the code-scan view: read the draft PR body and diff, then approve. The PR is opened as a draft and never merged.

scenarios.name: malicious-package
scenarios.title: Malicious open-source package
scenarios.summary: A widely used, long-abandoned package changes hands and ships a release that steals CI secrets. ci-runner-03 installed it: its install script posts the build environment to an external host, and the request carries a note addressed to AI security scanners asking them not to escalate.
walkthrough: Launch. The MAL advisory re-scores the graph; the exfiltration flow from ci-runner-03 enters the incident graph.
Open the incident: the payload's note to 'AI scanners' is flagged as a prompt injection and forced to escalate — it is shown as inert text.
Approve isolating ci-runner-03 (10.20.8.30).
Approve the supply-chain remediation for the package; review its reach on the map.
